properties.description:
Thirteen checks in two places. Six unit tests in `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/handshake.rs` pin the logic: the negotiation rule mirrored from rmcp, the revision threshold (`2024-11-05` and `2025-03-26` report as NOT having `structuredContent`; `2025-06-18` and later do, `>=` not `==`), the sidecar path beside its siblings, a file round trip, and that an unwritable path is survived rather than propagated — a diagnostic must never be able to fail a handshake.

Seven checks in `tools/smoke_mcp.py` drive the REAL BINARY over stdio, which is the only layer that proves the file is actually written during `initialize`: the sidecar exists, names the client, records what it asked for and what was settled, and — the one that matters — that **the negotiated version came from the exchange rather than from nowhere**, asserted as `negotiated ∈ {client_requested, server_offers}`.

⭐ ONE CHECK EXISTS FOR A REASON THAT IS NOT ABOUT CODE. `it disclaims the reading it would otherwise invite` asserts the file's own `note` contains the sentence saying `protocol_has_structured_content` does NOT mean the client reads it. The file is meant to be pasted into a field report and read by somebody who has never seen this module, so its self-description has to hold up alone. Naming that field `supports_structured_content` would have asserted the one thing it cannot know.

VERIFIED LIVE, not only by tests: the server was restarted against this session's real client and wrote `client-name: claude-code, version 2.1.241, requested and negotiated 2025-11-25, protocol_has_structured_content: true`. That is also the first data point for the comparison the file exists to enable.
properties.findings:
GREEN, read from cargo's OWN exit code: `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` exit 0, 165 suites, 1862 passed, 0 failed. `smoke_mcp.py` exit 0 with all seven handshake checks passing against the real binary over stdio.

🛑 THE FIRST RUN WAS RED AND THE NOTIFICATION SAID OTHERWISE. The background task reported "exit code 0" — that was the shell wrapper; cargo's own code was 101 and one test had failed. Believing the wrapper would have shipped over a red suite. Same family as the piped-gate trap, in a new costume: read the exit code of the thing you ran, not of what ran it.

WHAT FAILED, and it was a real ordering mistake rather than a defect: `a_served_skill_is_byte_identical_to_its_source` compares the skill COMPILED INTO THE BINARY against the source on disk. `report-friction/SKILL.md` was edited after the last build, so the two diverged and the test caught exactly what it exists for. Rebuilt; that suite is 8/8 and the workspace is green. **A served-skill edit needs a rebuild before the suite means anything** — the sibling of "format before baselining".

VERIFIED LIVE as well as by tests: the shared server was restarted against this session's real client and wrote `claude-code 2.1.241, requested and negotiated 2025-11-25, protocol_has_structured_content: true`. That is the comparison point the file exists to produce — a client that negotiates a modern revision AND reads structuredContent, against which Alex's report can be read.
properties.name: The handshake sidecar is written, and does not overclaim
